name: Libyan Arabic

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Libyan Arabic (liby1240).

notes: Skeleton. Libyan (Sulaymitic Maghrebi) Arabic, a Semitic (Afroasiatic) variety written in the Arabic abjad. Consonant letters are mapped to IPA; qāf ⟨ق⟩ has the voiced velar reflex [ɡ] typical of the Bedouin-type dialect, jīm ⟨ج⟩ is [dʒ], and the interdentals ⟨ث ذ ظ⟩ are retained. Short vowels are not written in the abjad and, apart from optional harakāt, are left unencoded; gemination and stress are not recovered, so a high omission score is expected. CONFUSABLE AND FORMATTING CODEPOINTS: three Unicode characters that occur in real Arabic-script text had no grapheme entry anywhere in this family, and a character with no entry is dropped without an error, so every occurrence was deleted in silence. ک KEHEH is the Persian/Urdu/Sindhi shape of kaf (annotated '= kaf mashkula') and is read here exactly as ك — [k]. ی FARSI YEH is annotated for Arabic as well as Persian, Urdu and Kashmiri, and is read exactly as ي — [j] or the mater lectionis [iː]. ـ TATWEEL is the kashida, inserted to stretch a word for justification and carrying no sound, so it maps to the empty string: the deletion is now stated instead of accidental, the treatment ٱ ALEF WASLA already had. ہ HEH GOAL is deliberately NOT added — Unicode assigns it to Urdu, and it occurs in none of the Arabic gold. The alternates are listed as bare letters only; a keheh or farsi yeh carrying a harakat does not match the diacritised digraph keys and falls back to the bare letter plus the mark, which yields the same phonemes. MEASURED UNDECIDABLE-INPUT CEILING. Not one of the 166 WikiPron ayl_arab_broad input words carries a single ḥaraka — no fatḥa, ḍamma, kasra, tanwīn, shadda or sukūn occurs anywhere on the orthographic side of this gold — while the gold transcriptions are fully vocalised: 23.8% of their phoneme segments are short vowels. Deleting every short vowel from the gold and rescoring with the harness's own scorer gives PER 0.1640 over 156 scored words (scripts/omission_score.py, which computes it through the scorer's own normalisation and edit distance), which is what a spec that emitted perfect consonants and long vowels and simply omitted the short vowels would score, and is therefore the omission score for this row. An omission score is not a lower bound. Deleting a segment and guessing it wrong cost the same single edit, so a spec that guesses the likeliest value beats omission whenever the guess lands, and rows do come in below it. The board row stands at 0.3055, so about 14.1 PER points separate the score from the omission score. That gap is rule error and is tractable; the omission score covers undecidable input that no grapheme table can recover. A gap above the omission score is a defect hypothesis, not an excuse: Hebrew sat above its own omission score for what looked like the same structural reason and the excess turned out to be a real defect, an unmapped geresh. That vocalisation and not the grapheme tables dominates the Arabic error is measured on the MSA row rather than inferred: ar scores PER 0.3139 on raw WikiPron and 0.1721 on the SAME gold with the input auto-diacritized (the wikipron_ar_diacritized row, wired in scripts/benchmark.py) — within a hundredth of the 0.1656 the spec scores on the material the orthography does supply, its folded PER, which scripts/folded_per.py computes and its valid_ceiling records. Vocalisation is worth about 14 PER points there, more than any grapheme-table change could be worth. No dialect row has such a companion: the diacritized loader is registered for ar alone, and wiring one for this row is the single highest-value follow-up available to it. It has to be labelled restored-MSA input rather than native vocalisation — the restorer targets MSA and Classical Arabic, so what it writes onto dialect orthography is an MSA reading, and a row scored against it measures the spec plus that assumption. MATRES LECTIONIS AFTER A CONSONANT. ⟨و⟩ and ⟨ي⟩ after a consonant letter are read first as the long vowels [uː] and [iː], then [oː] and [eː], then the glides [w] and [j]; word-initially and after a vowel they stay glides. Wikipedia 'Mater lectionis', section Arabic: "the almost invariable rule is that a long vowel is written with a mater lectionis and a short vowel with a diacritic symbol". Wikipedia 'Libyan Arabic' (source ayl_wikipedia), Note on transcription notation, gives oː as ō/او and eː as ē/اي, and Phonology says "The e and o vowels exist only in long form." Gold count (WikiPron ayl, 166 lines; rows with the letter after a consonant): ⟨و⟩ 49 rows, which hold uː 30, oː 5, w 13 segments; ⟨ي⟩ 48 rows, which hold iː 24, eː 6, j 10 segments. ADJACENT LETTERS AND THE FINAL TA MARBUTA. Read one letter at a time, the after_consonant rule made both letters of يو and وي long vowels (بيوت biːuːt), and it made ⟨و⟩ and ⟨ي⟩ before a final ة long vowels (قهوة with uː). The grapheme keys يو [juː, joː, iːw], وي [wiː, weː, uːj], ية [ja, jat], وة [wa, wat], وية [uːja, wja] and يوة [iːwa, eːwa, jwa] read the first of two adjacent letters as the glide, and a letter before a final ة as the glide. Gold count (WikiPron ayl, 166 lines): after a consonant letter, يو glide+long 1 (شليوني ʃaljoːni), long+glide 1 (شواشيو ʃwaːʃiːw); وي glide+long 1 (عوينة ʕweːna); no row reads both letters long. Word-final ية after a consonant letter: glide in 4 of 4 rows (جلابية ʒəlːaːbijːa). No Libyan source read here describes these sequences; the keys rest on the gold count. They cost 0.0006 PER against the pair keys alone (0.3049 to 0.3055) and are kept because the gold reads the glide.

sources.notes: Read (chart PDF). U+06A9 KEHEH is annotated '= kaf mashkula' and assigned to 'Persian, Urdu, Sindhi, ...'; U+06CC FARSI YEH is assigned to 'Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Kashmiri, ...'; U+0640 TATWEEL is '= kashida', 'inserted to stretch characters or to carry tashkil with no base letter'; U+06C1 HEH GOAL is assigned to Urdu only.

wikipron.measured: 0 of 166 wikipron input words (ayl_arab_broad.tsv) carry a haraka (short-vowel diacritic); Wiktionary files Arabic entries at the unvocalized page title (Wiktionary:About_Arabic / Wiktionary:Arabic_entry_guidelines, 'Entry name'), so the scraped input is a consonant-plus-long-vowel skeleton, exactly the pattern independently measured on the bare 'ar' wikipron row (0/17,563 words carry a haraka there; see ar.json audit.wikipron). No fold was run for this dialect row -- doing so needs the dialect's own vowel inventory, not MSA's -- so no valid_ceiling is recorded here; the wikipron_ar_diacritized loader (scripts/benchmark.py) that would supply it is wired for the 'ar' row only.
